title: City Council District 7
statement: Rockridge's commercial indicators show retail vitality at 11.89, but sentiment at -0.06 signals persistent friction that cannot be solved by throwing unmonitored municipal funds at the corridor. With Temescal Community Health Center holding $15,923,076.9 in operational funds and delivering care, my focus remains locked on verifiable fiscal oversight, auditing municipal service delivery, and demanding hard data before entertaining any new spending requests.

payload.text: Our canvass and corridor metrics confirm that while Rockridge retail vitality rose to 11.89, neighborhood sentiment dropped to -0.06 against the city benchmark of 0.020, with trajectory momentum slipping to 6 and 98 residents reported sick. Property crime sits at 39 and violent crime at 24. These figures reflect community friction rather than commercial collapse. I will not support unbudgeted corridor adjustments or open-ended funding without clear municipal performance audits and verified service baselines.

payload.note: Assessing commercial sentiment and service delivery following the recent dip in neighborhood sentiment.
